record.original_question: For a one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, if the first rational Čech cohomology group has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ, must the tiling have pure point spectrum?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.2 (Homological Pisot Conjecture). A one–dimensional, unimodular Pisot inflation tiling has pure point spectrum if its first rational Čech cohomology group has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be a one-dimensional, unimodular Pisot inflation tiling. That is, T is a tiling of the real line built from finitely many prototiles via a primitive substitution (inflation) rule with expansion factor λ > 1, where λ is a Pisot number (a real algebraic integer greater than 1 all of whose Galois conjugates lie strictly inside the unit disk) that is unimodular (its algebraic norm is ±1). Let Ω_T denote the associated tiling space (the orbit closure under translation of T in the local-matching topology), and let Ȟ¹(Ω_T; ℚ) denote its first Čech cohomology group with rational coefficients. The translation ℝ-action on Ω_T equipped with its unique invariant probability measure has an associated unitary representation on L²(Ω_T); this dynamical system is said to have pure point (pure discrete) spectrum if L²(Ω_T) is spanned by eigenfunctions of the translation action.

Question: If rank_ℚ Ȟ¹(Ω_T; ℚ) equals the algebraic degree of λ over ℚ, must the tiling dynamical system (Ω_T, ℝ) have pure point spectrum?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture as stated has been refuted. Barge, Bruin, Jones, and Sadun constructed one-dimensional unimodular Pisot substitution tilings whose first rational Čech cohomology has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ but whose tiling flows fail to have pure discrete spectrum (e.g., examples with coincidence rank 3 and norm divisible by 3, generalizing to every algebraic degree). This motivated the refined Coincidence Rank Conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Homological Pisot Substitutions and Exact Regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Examples of homological Pisot substitutions with coincidence rank 3 and norm divisible by 3 are constructed, with generalizations to every algebraic degree, whose tiling flows do not have pure discrete spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to the Homological Pisot Conjecture exist.

status_evidence.title: Factors of Pisot tiling spaces and the Coincidence Rank Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: After the original Homological Pisot Conjecture was disproven, the Coincidence Rank Conjecture was proposed as a refinement.
status_evidence.claim: The original conjecture was disproven; a refined conjecture (CRC) replaces it.
